paper.title: Low Temperature Co-Fired Ceramic Antenna for 35 GHz Applications with a Wideband GCPW to Stripline Transition
paper.abstract: In this paper we present the design, electromagnetic simulation and experimental results of a 35 GHz Low Temperature Co-Fired Ceramics (LTCC) antenna and a LTCC grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) to stripline (SL) transition. The stripline-fed antenna and the GCPW-to-SL transition are designed for a six-tape LTCC process. For characterization purposes, two back-to-back transitions are fabricated and measured, showing reflection losses lower than -10 dB between 27-46.7 GHz, and insertion losses lower than 1.5 dB in this frequency range. The insertion losses of the back-to-back transition are remarkably low in the whole Ka band (26.5-40 GHz), with estimated losses between 0.15-0.5 dB for a single transition. The antenna element has four parasitic microstrip patches and a simulated directivity of 8.2 dBi at 35 GHz. The antenna element integrated with the transition is fabricated and characterized on wafer. The integrated structure shows measured reflection losses lower than -10 dB between 34.48-36.39 GHz. The transmission characteristic as a function of frequency is recorded and in good agreement with the simulated gain. The overall size of the fabricated antenna with transition is 6.24 x 8.975 mm2, with the standalone antenna element having a size of just 6.24 x 6.15 mm2.

paper.title: Development and Experimental Results on LTCC Packages for Acoustic Wave Sensing Devices
paper.abstract: Novel LTCC packages intended for acoustic wave sensing devices chip assembly are proposed in this paper. A single assembly operation was required for both structure models based on DuPont 9K7 "green" tapes, after layout design and interactive 3-D electromagnetic optimization processes. Due to LTCC manufacturing technology, a large number of package structures containing cavities, inner vertical and horizontal interconnects, pads for inner components' assembly and external signal connections was manufactured. Surfaces acoustic wave (SAW) resonators and film bulk acoustic resonator (FBAR) structures have been used with very good results as temperature and, respectively, humidity sensing devices. Input and output signal ports have been define as coplanar transmission line (CPW) configuration for a good impedance matching to the measuring system. Linear behavior of the frequency shift vs. temperature and, respectively, relative humidity was evidenced. Although certain temperature sensitivity reduction is observed, an improved dynamic range of the return loss response is noticed for packaged SAW devices, favorable for subsequent signal processing and temperature value extracting. Very small and complex RF packages, with SMT compatible and solderable AgPt pinout and two different levels of Au pads for Au wire bonding inside the cavity intended to provide handling protection after wire bonding are the main outcome of this paper.

With twelve authors from four groups, nine of 31 references include at least one author (about 29%, in the 20-30% band): the Müller/Neculoiu GaN SAW and FBAR line ([14], [15], [18], [19], [20], [26]), the consortium chapter [21], and two conference versions of the present package work ([27], [31]). The package designs are backed by simulation figures and the lumped-model extraction. A reasonable applied packaging paper with appropriate, functional equations. Its standing is reduced by self-citation near the 30% threshold, careless reference numbering, and sensor results that are mostly qualitative.

paper.title: POCl3 Annealing Effect on The Flat Band Voltage Instabilities for a SiC Based MOS Capacitor at High Temperature
paper.abstract: The effect of post-oxidation annealing (POA) treatments on SiC based MOS capacitor characteristics have been investigated up to 623K, targeting operation in high temperature applications. In order to achieve the passivation of the SiO2/4H-SiC interface and to reduce flat band voltage (VFB) instabilities with temperature, the POA in POCl3 ambient was used. The structures subjected to POA were comparatively analysed with the as-oxidized ones. High frequency capacitance-voltage (C-V) measurements were performed both at room and high temperatures on wafer and encapsulated samples. The C-V characteristics show an improved stability of VFB with temperature for POCl3 based POA samples: while the as-oxidized structures show a linear decrease of VFB after 423 K, the POA leads to an increase of the temperature range where VFB is approximately constant (up to 623 K).

paper.title: A CMOS Imager for Time-of-Flight and Photon Counting Based on Single Photon Avalanche Diodes and In-Pixel Time-to-Digital Converters
paper.abstract: The design of a CMOS image sensor based on single-photon avalanche-diode (SPAD) array with in-pixel time-to-digital converter (TDC) is presented. The architecture of the imager is thoroughly described with emphasis on the characterization of the TDCs array. It is targeted for 3D image reconstruction. Several techniques as fast quenching/recharge circuit with tunable dead-time and time gated-operation are applied to reduce the noise and the power consumption. The chip was fabricated in a 0.18 um standard CMOS process and implements a double functionality: time-of-flight (ToF) estimation and photon counting. The imager features a programmable time resolution of the array of TDCs down to 145 ps. The measured accuracy of the minimum time bin is lower than +/-1LSB DNL and +/-1.7 LSB INL. The TDC jitter over the full dynamic range is less than 1 LSB.

paper.title: Integrated Dual-chain Dickson Charge Pump optimized for Resistive Loads
paper.abstract: The proposed circuit is a dual-chain Dickson type charge pump making use of both active and passive charge transfer switches in order to achieve a compromise between power efficiency, circuit complexity and device reliability. The charge pump is capable of sourcing up to 500 uA at 10 V output voltage for supplying the error amplifiers of two NMOS Low Drop Out (LDO) linear regulators as part of a high integration automotive IC.

paper.title: Beam Shaping for Phase Singularities
paper.abstract: In this paper we are molding the phase profile of a Gaussian beam in order to achieve a phase singularity called optical vortex. For this purpose, we apply the beam shaping technique for a 635 nm wavelength radiation using a diffractive optical element with high diffractive efficiency. We use reflective spiral phase plates and fork-like computer generated holograms, fabricated with photolithographic processes and electron beam lithography, respectively. Uniform ring intensity is achieved in the optical vortex configurations and also zero intensity where the phase is undefined. Phase singularities interferences are done using a Michelson interferometer. Beam shaping simulations results based on the Kirchhoff integral are in concordance with experimental results.

verdict.summary: Simulation, fabrication and optical characterisation of 8-level spiral phase plates and an EBL fork hologram for optical vortices; standard optics equations, clean citations, but several claims ('perfect reproducible', power conservation 'proved') outrun the evidence.

**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** Applies well-established vortex-generation methods ([21], [22], [24]) and standard diffraction simulation to fabricate and test devices; no new theory or algorithm.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 6 (angular momentum density, total angular momentum, J = S + L, diffraction integral, fork hologram intensity, SPP height profile)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate. Equations (4)-(6) are used to compute the simulated fields, the hologram pattern and the etch depths. Equations (1)-(3) are textbook background on the physical quantity the paper is about. They are not used afterwards, but they are physics rather than notation dressing up a programming operation, so they are not counted as necessity failures. They earn no quality bonus.

### Issues
The background equations contain errors: eq. (2) is labelled 'total orbital angular momentum' though it is the total angular momentum. The text refers to an 'equation (8)' that does not exist. The SPP amplitude is written exp(arctan(y'/x')) without the imaginary unit and topological charge.

---

## Citation Analysis

One of 24 references is a self-citation ([23], the CAS 2014 SPP fabrication paper, used for the mask figure); about 4%, relevant. No issues identified.

---

## Structural Analysis

The fabrication results are backed by WLI step heights (Tables 1-2), SEM and optical images, far-field captures and an interferogram. Several assertions go beyond the evidence: the process is called 'perfect reproducible' on the strength of an unquantified repeat; ring-intensity drops with m are said to 'prove' power conservation without any power measurement; 'perfect concordance' between mask and hologram is claimed from images alone. Simulation-experiment agreement is stated qualitatively, with no quantitative comparison, and diffraction efficiency is claimed in the abstract and conclusions but never measured. One limitation is acknowledged inline (the number of SPP levels is restricted by fabrication). The MATLAB simulation code is not released.

---

## Conclusion

A competent device-fabrication study with appropriate formalism and clean citation practice. Its structural quality is reduced by overclaiming and qualitative validation.

paper.title: Dielectric Sensing with Back-Gated Nanowires
paper.abstract: Extensive numerical calculations show that the capacitance of back-gated nanowires with various degrees of dielectric embeddings is accurately described with an effective dielectric constant as long as the difference between the dielectric thickness and the gate-nanowire distance is held constant. This is valid for dielectrics with permittivities ranging from simple air to water. However, due to screening the scaling is not valid if the dielectric lies down well below the nanowire. Moreover, when only the dielectric thickness varies the capacitance characteristics are S-shaped with three distinct regions, of which only the first two can be used for dielectric sensing. The first region is almost linear while the middle region, with a span of two diameters around the center of the nanowire, is the most sensitive.

flag_details.EXCESSIVE_SELF_CITATION: Seven of 23 references (30.4%) are by the authors: [11], [17], [21] (Boldeiu/Sandu/Moagar-Poladian) and [15], [16], [18], [20] (Sandu, on plasmon resonances and nanoantennas). [11] and [17] are directly relevant. [15], [16], [18], [20] and [21] concern plasmonic eigenmodes and are only methodologically linked through the Laplace equation (marginal similarity, about 0.3-0.5), which pushes the ratio just over 30%.

verdict.summary: ANSYS finite-element study of back-gate nanowire capacitance under partial dielectric embedding, with a textbook bipolar-coordinate derivation; technically sound and validated against prior work, but self-citation slightly exceeds 30%, partly through marginal plasmonics papers.

paper.title: High Temperature Compensated Voltage Reference Integrated Circuits on 4H-SiC Material
paper.abstract: This work demonstrates a functional fabricated high temperature compensated Voltage Reference (VR) integrated circuit on 4H-SiC material. The study starts with an experimental analysis on the feasibility on silicon carbide (SiC) of the widely used bandgap reference concept both with Schottky and bipolar diodes. Then an original solution is proposed for a special finger type MESFET. Our approach of the MESFET design overcomes the typical embedded drain leakage of finger type MESFET. This device design was specially developed for using in analog schematics on SiC. Further, an original VR schematic is proposed avoiding the bandgap reference topology and accordingly avoiding an operational amplifier (OpAmp), which is not yet developed on SiC. The performed measurements on the fabricated integrated circuits show a temperature coefficient (TC) comparable to the normal bandgap voltage references on silicon but this SiC circuit is able to work up to 300 C, compared to 125 C for silicon or 200 C for SOI (silicon on insulator). A very important progress of our work is the integration of the presented circuit on the same SiC chip with a power lateral MESFET. Additionally, the circuit contains a linear temperature sensor useful for over temperature protection.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Feasibility test of the bandgap-reference principle on 4H-SiC with Schottky and bipolar diodes (external OpAmp), followed by an OpAmp-less voltage-reference IC built from planar finger-gate SiC MESFETs, epitaxial resistors and Schottky diodes, measured up to 250-300 C and co-integrated with a power MESFET and a temperature sensor.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** Device and circuit engineering applying the classical PTAT/CTAT compensation principle and a new circuit arrangement in a different material; no new algorithm or formal model.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 5 (Shockley/thermionic diode law, its exponential approximation, inversion, PTAT difference, bandgap sum)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate. These are the textbook bandgap-reference relations behind the feasibility demonstration.

### Issues
Minor errors: the text says 'eq. (4) simplifies to' where eq. (1) is meant. The MESFET double pinch-off is referred to Fig. 1 instead of Fig. 2.

---

## Citation Analysis

Ten of 25 references (40%) are by the authors, spanning the group's SiC MESFET digital logic, isolation, Schottky-contact and voltage-reference papers, including two conference versions of this circuit ([11], [12]). All are topically related, so none counts as irrelevant, but the share exceeds the 30% threshold by a wide margin. Citation accuracy is weak: the qualified Schottky contact for the BepiColombo mission is attributed to [10] (a SiC NMOS regulator paper by another group) where [16] fits, and the integrated power MESFET is attributed to [9] (a bipolar OpAmp paper) where [24] fits.

---

## Structural Analysis

The circuit claims are supported by measured TC on three chips (15-33 ppm/C over 25-250 C), PSRR, line regulation, sensor linearity and power MESFET characteristics. The abstract's claim that the circuit works 'up to 300 C' rests only on a supply-current value at 300 C, while the measurement setup is described as reaching 250 C and the TC is reported to 250 C. The PSRR discrepancy and output-level drift versus simulation are acknowledged and given plausible causes, and the conclusion names the main limitation (MESFET gate leakage), so limitations are present inline. No SPICE models, layouts or data are released.

---

## Conclusion

A substantive SiC circuit demonstration with appropriate formalism. It is disqualified by self-citation well above 30% and weakened further by misdirected reference pointers and a stretched temperature claim.
